statement: rules/rules.json has ZERO entries with language=="k8s" (or any kubernetes-related content: no securityContext/runAsNonRoot/hostNetwork/privileged/RBAC/resource-limit rows). Grepping the repo (including the .mjs files under mcp/) for k8s/kubernetes detection logic also turns up nothing — there is no legacy source-policy-*.mjs for k8s to port; the only .mjs files in this repo are MCP server infra (mcp/rust-rules-mcp-*.mjs, mcp/ocentra-enforcer-mcp.mjs), unrelated to rule detection.
why: The arc-12 workpack says "Port the corresponding .mjs k8s/manifest detection logic to Rust validators" as if a legacy source exists in-tree, mirroring how arc-06/07/09 ported real source-policy-*.mjs files. For k8s there is no such source in this repo (it likely existed only in an older/parent repo, or was scoped as prose-only intent). A worker trusting the workpack's phrasing literally would waste time searching for a file that does not exist.
howToApply: Before assuming a workpack's "port the .mjs logic" instruction has a real source file to read, grep the whole repo (not just crates/ or rules/) for the family's domain keywords AND check `find . -iname '*.mjs'` for anything beyond mcp/ infra. If nothing turns up, treat the rule family as GREENFIELD: design the RuleId family (K8S-1..K8S-4 in this case) and its detection markers directly from RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md's description ("pod/security-context/RBAC/resource-limit shapes") and cite that as your authority instead of a nonexistent port source.

evidence.ref: grep -in 'k8s|kubernetes|securityContext|runAsNonRoot|hostNetwork|privileged|RBAC' rules/rules.json -> 0 hits; find / -iname '*.mjs' -> only mcp/*.mjs infra files, no source-policy-*.mjs anywhere in the tree

statement: enforcer-lang-common's src/pattern.rs exposes PatternValidator, a reusable single-line-substring-match Validator (fires on the FIRST line containing any of a fixed marker list). This is the correct engine to depend on for a brand-new lang-family crate with no existing rules.json rows, rather than duplicating the TS crate's RuleSpec/SpecValidator/text_scan machinery (which adds word-boundary/comment-guard logic irrelevant to YAML key:value line scanning). enforcer-lang-security's SEC-2 family already depends on enforcer-lang-common only for this engine (not its rule bodies) -- that is the sanctioned reuse pattern to follow, not copy-pasting the TS crate's spec.rs.
why: Without checking enforcer-lang-common's charter doc comment (crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/lib.rs), it is easy to assume every lang crate must own its own from-scratch text-matching primitives (the way enforcer-lang-ts's text_scan.rs does), leading to duplicated word-boundary/comment-skip code that YAML manifests do not need (YAML keys like `privileged:` are not identifiers you need word-boundary guards against, and manifests rarely embed the marker inside a comment in a way that matters for this rule family).
howToApply: Before writing a new lang-family crate's detection primitives from scratch, read enforcer-lang-common's lib.rs charter comment and src/pattern.rs -- if the new family's detection shape is "does this line contain literal substring X" (true for K8S's YAML key:value scan), depend on enforcer-lang-common's PatternValidator directly instead of reimplementing SpecValidator/RuleSpec/text_scan. Only build bespoke matching primitives when the family needs word-boundary or comment-guard semantics PatternValidator does not provide.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/pattern.rs PatternValidator::validate (single literal-substring line scan); crates/enforcer-lang-common/src/lib.rs charter comment names SEC-2 as an existing engine-only consumer

statement: The coordination hub's write-lock claim for exact path 'Cargo.toml'/'Cargo.lock' at repo root can be held by a sibling arc lane (arc-11 held it during arc-12's session) even though this workspace's root Cargo.toml declares `members = ["crates/*"]` (a glob) -- meaning a brand-new crate directory is auto-discovered by cargo WITHOUT any edit to root Cargo.toml at all. Only Cargo.lock changes (regenerated by `cargo build`/`cargo test`), and that file's claim can succeed independently once the sibling lane releases it, without ever needing to touch or wait on root Cargo.toml.
why: A worker that assumes it must edit root Cargo.toml to register a new workspace member (the pattern in many non-glob Cargo workspaces) would either block indefinitely waiting for a lock on a file it does not actually need to write, or attempt an unnecessary edit that risks a real merge conflict with a sibling lane's concurrent Cargo.lock/Cargo.toml claim.
howToApply: Before claiming root Cargo.toml for a new-crate workpack, check `[workspace] members` in the root Cargo.toml -- if it is a glob (`crates/*`), you only need `Cargo.lock` (regenerated automatically), not `Cargo.toml` itself. Claim only Cargo.lock at integration time; skip claiming/editing Cargo.toml entirely.

evidence.ref: root Cargo.toml: [workspace] members = ["crates/*"]; coordination_claim on crates/enforcer-lang-k8s/cargo.toml + root cargo.toml + cargo.lock returned write-lock-conflict on 'cargo.toml' (owned by arc-11) even though the new crate's own Cargo.toml claim path succeeded once root cargo.toml/cargo.lock were dropped from the same request
